newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian arrested for defaming Suharto.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian arrested for defaming Suharto.

text.p: The private secretary of an Indonesian writer whose book has just been banned has been arrested and charged with helping to publish material defamatory of President Suharto, one of his lawyers said on Thursday.
Lawyer Paskah Irianto told Reuters that his client, Buyung Rachmat Buchori Nasution, was arrested on Wednesday at his house.
"He was charged with defaming the president and vice president which carries a maximum penalty of one year and four months in jail," the lawyer said.

Nasution is the private secretary of Soebadio Sastrosatomo, former chairman of the defunct Indonesian Socialist Party (PSI), who recently published a book entitled "New Era, New Leader - (Soe)Badio Rejects the Engineering by the New Order Regime".
The New Order is the term used to describe the government of Suharto, who rose to power in the wake of a 1965 coup blamed on the banned Indonesian Communist Party.
The 50-page book sold widely before being banned this month.
Irianto said it was not clear if police would press charges against Sastrosatomo, adding that Nasution was still held at police headquarters.
"Frankly speaking, it is a little bit strange because Nasution is only the secretary and not the writer," he said.
The Attorney-General's office questioned Sastrosatomo over the book's contents but no charges have been laid.
Ali Sadikin, a former Jakarta governor and leading government critic, as well as a retired diplomat, Yusuf Ronodipuro, have been questioned over the book.
The Kompas newspaper on Thursday quoted police sources as saying they were searching for people who printed and distributed the book. It gave no further details.
The PSI was one of many political parties that flourished during Indonesia's brief period of parliamentary democracy in the 1950s.
In the 1970s, most non-government parties were forced to amalgamate into the Moslem-oriented United Development Party (PPP) and the Christian Nationalist Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI).
Only the ruling Golkar party, the PPP and PDI will be recognised when Indonesia goes to the polls on May 29.
Political analysts say Suharto is curbing any signs of opposition ahead of the elections, which Golkar is determined to win.
